summary: This sermon explains that humans are spiritually dead because of sin dating back to the Garden of Eden and desperately need a Savior. Using the parable of the Pharisee and tax collector, the pastor emphasizes that self-righteousness cannot save us; rather, humble repentance and faith in Jesus Christ brings salvation by God's grace, not by our works or moral performance.
key_points: Humanity became spiritually dead at the fall in Eden and needs a Savior to reconnect with God
Self-righteous rule-keeping (the Pharisee) does not justify us before God
Humble repentance and recognition of our need (the tax collector) leads to justification
Salvation comes by grace through faith alone, not by works
True salvation produces transformation and good works as a result
big_idea: Salvation is God's gift of grace that rescues us from spiritual death and sin through faith in Jesus Christ, transforming us from the inside out—not through our own moral efforts or self-righteousness.
title: We Are the Church: SALVATION
